title: What if Earth's magnetic field switched off? 🧲
subject: magnetosphere
description:
Would you rather lose the magnetic field or the ozone layer? 👇

What would happen if Earth's magnetic field disappeared? 41,000 years ago, during the Laschamp event, it fell to about 5% of today's strength. Mars shows what a planet without a global field looks like over billions of years.

Sources: University of Oulu / Journal of Geophysical Research: Space Physics (Laschamp excursion, 2026), University of Michigan via Space.com ("41,000 years ago, auroras blazed near the equator"), NASA MAVEN mission (Spaceflight Now, 2015), Wikipedia ("South Atlantic Anomaly")
tags: what if earth lost its magnetic field
what if the magnetic field disappeared

scenes.text: Picture the northern lights over the equator.
Models suggest it happened 41,000 years ago, when Earth's magnetic field fell to 5 percent.
Switch it off completely, and the solar wind slams into the upper air.
Even now, Hubble turns off its UV detectors over one weak spot, the South Atlantic Anomaly.
Over millions of years, the air could leak away. NASA's MAVEN probe measured Mars losing 100 grams of atmosphere a second.
Earth's field isn't vanishing, but it weakened about 9 percent in 200 years.
